title: Full-Time Cloth Nappy Package – 24 Nappies + 24 Inserts + Boosters + Wet Bags $499.99 (RRP $872.49, 43% off) @ Waladi
body:
Deal: Full-Time Cloth Nappy Package – 24 Nappies + 24 Inserts + Boosters + Wet Bags $499.99 (RRP $872.49, 43% off) @ Waladi

[GreenLego] I have no ideal about nappies, but are these the same as ones you get on aliexpress for $140?
https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005005167573945.html
plus whatever the extra addons included in this post.
[LuckyDrew] Can confirm buying these from AliExpress is the move. We’re past that stage now thankfully but sure as heck didn’t pay $499. And 24 is a lot. People plan to go full cloth but the reality usually is a mix at best.
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] I wouldn't buy clothes from aliexpress, let alone for your baby. I can't speak for the quality of that link however have you seen the documentaries about dangerous chemicals, pfas and flammability with some clothing products from AliExpress when they're thoroughly tested?
[GreenLego] But then, where do you buy your clothes from? Pretty much all clothing come from China now days?
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] Ones associated with Australian retailers that are tested for compliance. If you haven't gone there yet Uniqlo is the best.
[ProlapsedHeinous] At least through a retailer you have redress for issues. I don't think its worth the risk for bubs
[Disabled-User] Members joining just to upvote. Must be a good deal.
[kerfuffle] That only applies to one user; the other user has been here for a number of years now
[seug123] try the classifieds section of the onion
[Harvey1] There is no world where cloth nappies cost over $800 RRP. Nice try.
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] Have you bought cloth nappies before? This is a very low price. A decent quality set can be $1500 on sale. Scarily, that is cheap too compared to disposables. Can't speak for the quality of this brand though.
[husky2026] Agree. Also i feel like to use cloth full time you need more than 24 nappies allowing time to dry..etc so cost can go beyond the $500 easy
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] Totally agree. Highly recommend cloth fulltime hey, if possible. Definitely still good to have spare disposables too though.
[Zephyrus] Where on earth are you buying them? Where is a set of 24 costing $1500?
That's $62 a nappy. You can easily get cloth nappies for under $20 each
[Mickey333] RRP - Rot & Rest in Peace lmao. Oh wait, this $800 shitbag is made of pure handcrafted silk
[husky2026] I think this is a decent price, the quality is great and price wise is still cheaper than many other brand available in the market. The charcoal inserts from waladi brand is superior to all the other ones we've seen. i would recommend the waladi brand for cloth nappies anyday. Happy flute is also ok especially considering the price difference but wont be the majority of our stack and definetly not an overnight nappy for us, second would be mimi nappies but i feel they're a bit overpriced. If you're new to cloth nappies better try 2-3 brands first and find the one that best fits then buy a package like this as every baby is different.
[huuuuugo] Please excuse my ignorance, but how does this work?
Do you like scrape the baby poop off somehow and then wash the nappies by hand? (I wouldn't want to contaminate my washing machine with this.) Also, wouldn't the moisture stay close to the skin, unlike the single-use ones which are designed to keep the moisture away from the skin?
Just to clarify, I have a 12 months old at home, and despite being environmentally conscious, I can not, for the love of god, imagine hand washing nappies every day, on top of all else you need to do for a baby every day already.
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] There a whole system of how to do it hygienically like washing every day nappies (stored in wet pale to air) with a hot prewash at the end of the day and a big hot main wash every 3 days of all those prewashes. You can scrape poo off the nappy the same was you would with and adult, toilet paper, or you could wash it off. They absorb very well, especially when you use the additional bamboo inserts as bub gets bigger. You can customise the absorption and fit as they grow.
If life is hard enough as it is honestly just survival using disposables is totally okay however washing reuseables is significantly cheaper in the long run, especially if you have multiple children and might be nicer on their skin if they are having issues. Yes, it is definitely more work for you at the end of the day and you can't do it half-arsed so to speak, or they'll get mouldy (if they're not airing or left too long) or be unhygienic (not washed hot enough) or delaminate (washed too hot).
There are Facebook groups which go through it all. If you're interested I can pass these on? Some of the brands might give their recommendations on how best to clean them but normally similar.
If what you're doing is working though and you're happy, just stick with it. 12 months is an exciting time, all the best!
[mrtin] You roll the poo into the toilet afterwards. Wash seperately in washing machine. It's not bad.
Even if you have 1 (or go part time) , you will save so many disposable nappies going into landfill. Giveit a go! If everyome had just 1, we'd save millions of nappies going into landfill.
[maxwellian] You'll find the 'wicking' does differ as the disposables have been made far too comfortable to wear while soiled, reusable makes toilet training so much easier/earlier.
[Hitokage] Was skeptical in the beginning, but it works out quite easily for us and our 2 month old. We use disposables when out, and reusables at home. Seems to be making a difference, bub seemed to be on the verge of getting red and rashy when on disposables; got better after switching to reusables.
We bought a bidet hose to spray off the poo rather than scrape it off.
[ProlapsedHeinous] just buy a dedicated second turdtumbler for the buttnuggz
